Pre-Incorporation & Know-Your-Customer

UBO Ultimate Beneficial Owner Screening Rules Official Registry Only

>=25% ownership / control

Applicable AML statute: Law 10/2010 of 28 April on the prevention of money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended; Royal Decree 304/2014 of 5 May approving its implementing regulation; Royal Decree 609/2023 of 11 July establishing the Central Register of Beneficial Ownership (Registro Central de Titularidades Reales); Spanish Companies Act, Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010 of 2 July; applicable EU AML legislation, including Directive (EU) 2015/849 as amended. The Central Register of Beneficial Ownership is administered through the Ministry of Justice and receives relevant information from the Commercial Registry, notarial databases and other competent sources.
Registered Agent & Physical Address Licensed Agent Required

A virtual office may be acceptable for initial corporate registration if it is a genuine service address, the company can receive official notices, the landlord authorizes use and the address is not fictitious. It is not a substitute for operational substance. Cross-border road freight requires evidence of effective and stable establishment, access to transport records, a transport manager, financial standing, professional competence, vehicles or lawful access to vehicles and premises appropriate to the licensed operation. A mailbox-only arrangement creates elevated licensing, banking, tax-residence and AML risk.

✓ Partner licensed company-secretary channels provide local registered address and government mail forwarding.

Stage 03

Tax Identity & Indirect Tax

Tax authority e-portal, entity tax classification elections, VAT thresholds, and 0% export documentation chain.

Tax ID Application Infrastructure

Competent tax authority

Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) — Sede Electrónica: https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es

E-government filing portal

Spanish SL: after notarial incorporation and Commercial Registry registration, file Modelo 036 to obtain the definitive NIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal); a provisional NIF is granted immediately and remains valid for 6 months, convertible to a definitive NIF once incorporation documents are filed with the registry. Foreign non-resident entities carrying out taxable Spanish operations must appoint a Spanish tax representative and file Modelo 036 (or Modelo 030 in some procedures) to obtain a non-resident NIF (NIF-NR); this single identifier is used for VAT, corporate/income tax, and customs clearance purposes, and must be quoted on all invoices and customs declarations.

Tax ID type & application path: Entity_Level_Taxation — the ES_SL is a resident corporate entity subject to Impuesto sobre Sociedades (Spanish Corporate Income Tax) at the standard 25% rate on worldwide income. No pass-through regime applies to a Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada. A non-resident entity without a permanent establishment is taxed only on Spanish-source income under Impuesto sobre la Renta de No Residentes (IRNR). — Spanish SL: after notarial incorporation and Commercial Registry registration, file Modelo 036 to obtain the definitive NIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal); a provisional NIF is granted immediately and remains valid for 6 months, convertible to a definitive NIF once incorporation documents are filed with the registry. Foreign non-resident entities carrying out taxable Spanish operations must appoint a Spanish tax representative and file Modelo 036 (or Modelo 030 in some procedures) to obtain a non-resident NIF (NIF-NR); this single identifier is used for VAT, corporate/income tax, and customs clearance purposes, and must be quoted on all invoices and customs declarations.

Default Tax Classification & Elections

Default tax classification

Entity_Level_Taxation — the ES_SL is a resident corporate entity subject to Impuesto sobre Sociedades (Spanish Corporate Income Tax) at the standard 25% rate on worldwide income. No pass-through regime applies to a Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada. A non-resident entity without a permanent establishment is taxed only on Spanish-source income under Impuesto sobre la Renta de No Residentes (IRNR).

Available election forms

Spain does not provide a check-the-box election. Available statutory elections include: (i) consolidated corporate tax group regime (régimen de consolidación fiscal, requiring ≥70% voting rights and a tax consolidation agreement approved by AEAT); (ii) special SME incentives and reduced rates (e.g., newly created entities at 15% for first year); (iii) patent box regime at reduced effective rates for qualifying IP; (iv) UTE/transparent joint venture elections; (v) optional application of the foreign PE exemption method. EU ATAD anti-hybrid rules (transposed by Law 4/2021) override elective outcomes, and no elective hybrid instrument is available for the TIR trucking vehicle.

VAT / GST & 0% Export Zero-Rating

Standard VAT / GST rate

21%

Mandatory registration threshold (Nexus)

No general turnover exemption threshold for entities established in Spain: any person effecting taxable supplies must register for IVA from the first euro. For non-established EU and non-EU hauliers, B2B transport services are generally subject to the reverse charge in Spain, avoiding mandatory registration; full Spanish VAT registration is triggered by domestic B2C passenger/transport services, local acquisitions of fuel or goods, or intra-Community distance sales exceeding EUR 10,000 per calendar year (EU-wide threshold). Non-EU businesses acquiring goods or services subject to Spanish VAT must register through a tax representative unless an exception applies.

Export 0% zero-rating conditions

Goods exported to destinations outside the EU qualify for 0% VAT (exemption with credit) where the exporter is identified for Spanish VAT, the goods physically leave EU customs territory within 3 months from dispatch (extendable by AEAT), and proof of exit is retained. Overland TIR operations to non-EU territories qualify as export transport when the TIR carnet is stamped by the customs office of departure and exit; international transport of goods and ancillary services directly linked to export (including the overland leg under TIR) are zero-rated under Article 21 of Ley 37/1992. Intra-Community dispatches follow a separate exemption regime (Article 25) requiring the customer's EU VAT ID and periodic recapitulative statements.

  • DUA (Documento Único Administrativo) — customs export declaration with accepted exit summary confirmation
  • Carnet TIR (Carnet TIR) duly stamped by the customs office of departure and the customs office of exit
  • CMR consignment note signed by the carrier and consignee
  • Commercial invoice issued by the exporter
  • Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT MT103 evidencing receipt of export proceeds into a Spanish bank account
  • Proof of physical exit: customs exit stamp, port/terminal loading receipt, or electronic exit records from the customs system
  • Transport insurance policy or equivalent risk documentation (supporting evidence in tax audit)

Mandatory e-invoicing under Act 18/2022 ('Crea y Crece') requires interoperable structured electronic invoices between businesses; the 'Verifactu' system requires billing software to produce tamper-evident sequential records with SHA-256 hash chaining and optional QR code, delivering records to AEAT upon request. Large taxpayers (annual turnover > EUR 8,000,000) and VAT group members must submit transaction-level records to AEAT under SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información) within 4 calendar days for received invoices and 8 calendar days for issued invoices. Spain does not operate a government real-time clearance or digital stamping model; the SII is a near-real-time reporting regime rather than a pre-clearance authorization.

Export support documentation must be retained for at least 4 years (6 years where capital-gain or rebate claims apply) and produced to AEAT during audit; if exit is not substantiated within the applicable term, the exporter must self-assess output VAT plus late-payment interest (Article 21.3 Ley 37/1992). Incorrect or fraudulent zero-rating claims attract a penalty of 50%-150% of the tax amount under Article 191 Ley General Tributaria, loss of the zero-rating benefit, and publication sanctions. Criminal liability for tax fraud (Article 305 Código Penal) arises where the defrauded tax exceeds EUR 120,000, punishable by imprisonment of 1 to 5 years and fines of up to 6 times the defrauded amount, with retrospective clawbacks extending under the 4-year prescription rules.

Stage 04

Banking & Treasury Architecture

Central-bank FX diagnosis, tier-1 local banks vs offshore digital EMI matrix, and KYC rejection defense guide.

Foreign Exchange Regime & Central Bank Policy

Current-account convertibility

Spain, as a Member State of the Eurozone and the EU, maintains full convertibility for both current account and capital account transactions under the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (Articles 63–66 TFEU). There is no exchange control approval requirement for profit remittances by non-resident shareholders, dividend distributions, repatriation of liquidation proceeds or service payments. Remittances must comply with tax reporting (Modelo 296 withholding certificate), corporate income tax compliance, and, for statistical purposes, the Spanish balance-of-payments declaration to Banco de España. Special review applies only in restricted sectors (defense, media, critical infrastructure, real estate for non-EU/EFTA investors) under Regulation 8/2023, which is unlikely to apply to a road freight holding vehicle.

Export proceeds surrender rules

There are no mandatory export proceeds surrender rules and no foreign exchange conversion requirements for Spanish export companies. Exporters are free to retain receivables in foreign currency (e.g., USD, GBP) and may invoice in any currency under the principle of contractual freedom. For freight services rendered under TIR carnets, the transport operator must keep a commercial dossier including CMR notes, TIR carnet certificates and customs export declarations (DUA) to substantiate the euro or non-euro proceeds in bank filings; all export and service proceeds are subject only to standard anti-money laundering reporting thresholds (€10,000 cash or equivalent) and statistical reporting in the annual balance-of-payments declaration.

Central bank supervision: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), in coordination with the Ministry of Economic Affairs and Digital Transformation (Dirección General de Política Comercial e Inversiones, DGPCII) and the Executive Service of the Commission for the Prevention of Money Laundering (SEPBLAC), administers monetary, exchange control and AML/KYC supervision in Spain.

Offshore Digital Bank / EMI Whitelist

Cross-border EMI / Fintech rails Fit: High

EU/EEA passporting Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) are viable only as a complementary payment mechanism for the SL, rated Medium viability with strict onboarding constraints. An EMI authorized under the Electronic Money Directive (2009/110/EC) in Spain or passported into Spain may hold segregated funds, issue IBANs and execute SEPA transfers without credit institution status; however, an EMI cannot provide non-EEA domestic clearing, letters of credit, or over-the-counter FX derivative products without an additional investment firm license. For bonded cross-border trucking, an EMI is suitable for fuel card clearing and sub-account segregation, but statutory driver salary payments and TIR customs guarantee balances must be maintained with a fully licensed Spanish credit institution.

Core KYC Rejection Triggers & Defense Dossier

Non-resident corporate shareholder structure with multi-country beneficial owners

Root cause: Non-resident corporate shareholder structure with multi-country beneficial owners

Defense evidence: Provide full chain ownership notarized and apostilled register of ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) with Spanish tax identification number (NIF) or passport copies; audited financial statements of the parent; declaration of source of wealth (privacidad patrimonial); notarial certificate of the SL's share transfers for at least 36 months; and contractual explanation of the TIR freight operations, including list of logistics clients.
Industry activity flagged as high-risk due to wholesale fuel purchases and cross-border cash advances to truck drivers

Root cause: Industry activity flagged as high-risk due to wholesale fuel purchases and cross-border cash advances to truck drivers

Defense evidence: Provide the operator's ISO 9001 or ISO 28000 certificate; Spanish Ministry of Transport carrier's license; TIR carnet issuer certificate (Asociación del Transporte Internacional por Carretera – ASTIC); signed fuel supply agreements with branded Spanish refineries; driver salary payroll data with tax/SEPE filings; and a documented fleet anti-money-laundering manual incorporating cash advance limits at €500 per driver per week.
Cross-border payments to non-EU jurisdictions for road tolls, roadside assistance, and bunker fuel

Root cause: Cross-border payments to non-EU jurisdictions for road tolls, roadside assistance, and bunker fuel

Defense evidence: Establish a treasury policy identifying only necessary payments for transport operation, using a pre-approved beneficiary whitelist, underlying invoices with number/date/value; provide customs-approved CMR and TIR carnet photocopies for each transit; track freight invoices (facturas) under the Spanish electronic invoicing requirement; and sign SWIFT MT103 with beneficiary bank verification from SWIFT/IBAN directory.

Cross-Border Clearing Corridors & Settlement Fit

Initial subscriber capital and subsequent equity injections into the SL must be routed via SWIFT MT103 from the non-resident shareholder's bank to the SL's Tier 1 Spanish bank using the Spanish NIF of the company and the IBAN of the capital account. The payment must carry the appropriate ECB Statistical Purpose Code (e.g., 'eq_cap' / 'P01' for subscribed capital) or the Banco de España balance-of-payments category 'Direct Investment – Equity Capital.' For equity contributions above €1,500,000 by EU shareholders, a post-investment declaration may be required; for non-EU/EFTA shareholders, foreign investment filing to DGPCII is required if the amount exceeds €1,000,000 or if the SL engages in regulated sectors. The bank will request the notarial deed of capital increase (escritura de aumento de capital) or the SL's certificate of definitive payment (certificado de desembolso) before allowing disposition of the injected funds.Outbound trade and treasury disbursements are executed through: (a) SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) for EUR payments to EU beneficiaries with IBAN for driver salary, fuel, road tolls and routine vendor invoices; (b) SWIFT MT103 for non-EU USD/EUR vendor settlements and TIR carnet guarantee recharges; (c) documentary letters of credit (UCP 600) issued in favor of fuel distributors for bulk diesel purchases exceeding €25,000 per draw; (d) internal cash-pooling structures between the SL's accounts and subsidiaries using ISAE 3402-audited treasury platforms. Fuel card clearing is sourced through branded cards (e.g., DKV, UTA, Routex) that use a three-party payment network with next-day settlement to service stations and a monthly aggregated VAT invoice, which in turn is settled from the SL's operating account.FX Forwards (Spot-deferred): EUR/USD and EUR/GBP outright forwards with maturities up to 12 months, used to hedge non-euro TIR freight rates and fuel costs.Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs): for emerging-market currencies encountered on transit routes through Turkey, Russia/Central Asia or the Middle East, only if the counterparty is a regulated Spanish/EU bank offering NDFs with settlement in EUR because those currencies are not freely deliverable in Spain.Cross-Currency Swaps (XCCY): to swap USD committed receivables from non-EU logistics clients into EUR fixing margin, subject to the bank's ISDA/CSA arrangement and the SL's ability to post cash collateral.OTC FX Options: permissible only if the SL has a demonstrable commercial hedging need and the account relationship exceeds €5 million annual turnover; the bank will require the underlying freight invoice pipeline to prove commercial purpose and ensure MiFID retail leverage restrictions do not apply.

E-commerce / gateway settlement fit: EU/EEA passporting Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) are viable only as a complementary payment mechanism for the SL, rated Medium viability with strict onboarding constraints. An EMI authorized under the Electronic Money Directive (2009/110/EC) in Spain or passported into Spain may hold segregated funds, issue IBANs and execute SEPA transfers without credit institution status; however, an EMI cannot provide non-EEA domestic clearing, letters of credit, or over-the-counter FX derivative products without an additional investment firm license. For bonded cross-border trucking, an EMI is suitable for fuel card clearing and sub-account segregation, but statutory driver salary payments and TIR customs guarantee balances must be maintained with a fully licensed Spanish credit institution.

Annual Third-Party Transaction Information Return (Modelo 347) January 1 through the last calendar day of February (February 28/29) following the tax year-end; mandatory when transactions with one counterparty exceed EUR 3,005.06 $0 USD Informative-return penalties: EUR 20 per false or omitted data item, minimum EUR 300, maximum EUR 20,000; EUR 200 flat for late filing; no strike-off.
Corporate Income Tax Return (Impuesto sobre Sociedades - Modelo 200) Within 25 calendar days following the 6-month period after tax year-end; for calendar-year entity, July 1 to July 25 $0 USD Late-payment surcharges of 5%-20% plus interest; false or incomplete data attract penalties up to 150% of the tax due; registral strike-off does not apply.
Annual Accounts Deposit (Depósito de Cuentas Anuales) Shareholders' meeting to approve annual accounts within 6 months of fiscal year-end (by June 30 for calendar-year entity); deposit within 1 month of approval, in practice by July 30/31 $50 USD Registral closure: no corporate act (capital increase, director appointment, branch registration) may be recorded until deposit is made; fines of EUR 1,800-18,000, capped at 2% of equity; directors may be personally liable.
Annual Beneficial Ownership Declaration (Declaración Anual de Titularidad Real) Annually within 1 month of the general meeting approving the annual accounts; for calendar-year entities, in practice by July 30/31; also updated upon qualifying share transfers $0 USD Registral closure of subsequent corporate filings; administrative fines for false, incomplete, or untimely UBO information under AML Law 10/2010; no strike-off.
Annual return deadline

Within 4 months following fiscal year-end; for calendar-year entity, by April 30

Statutory government annual fee

$30 USD

Late filing penalties

Books lack evidentiary value in commercial litigation; registry may impose penalties under Commercial Registry Regulations; no administrative strike-off.

Strike-off trigger

Turnover: Mandatory independent audit for two consecutive fiscal years when the company meets at least two of the following thresholds: total assets exceed EUR 2,850,000; net annual turnover exceeds EUR 5,700,000; average workforce exceeds 50 employees. Stage 06

Corporate Tax & Transfer Pricing

Corporate income tax (CIT), box-by-box return breakdown, dividend WHT, and director personal liability.

Statutory corporate income tax (CIT)

25% (Article 29.1, Law 27/2014 on Corporate Income Tax)

Dividend withholding tax (WHT)

19% withholding tax on dividends distributed by the Spanish SL to non-resident beneficial owners without a permanent establishment in Spain; 0% may apply under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive where the shareholder holds at least 5% of the capital for at least one year; DTA rates may reduce or eliminate the domestic rate.

Mandatory Return Breakdown

Deadline: · Frequency:

Within 25 calendar days after the expiry of six months following the end of the tax period (Article 124 LIS); for a 31 December year-end the filing window is 1-25 July.

Box-by-Box Return Breakdown (non-resident focus)

BoxField Non-resident guidanceTax-evasion pitfall
Modelo 200, Page 1, Box 00100 (Identification) SL tax identification number (NIF), corporate name, registered office, legal form code, CNAE activity code for long-haul bonded freight transport under TIR Carnets, fiscal year start and end dates. The Spanish SL must use its own Spanish NIF. Non-resident beneficial owners must be disclosed in the shareholders annex and are not entered as filers on Modelo 200. Late filing before an AEAT demand triggers surcharges of 5% within three months, 10% after three to six months, 15% after six to twelve months, and 20% after twelve months plus default interest. Deliberate non-filing or under-filing is an infringement under Article 191 LGT and attracts proportional penalties of 50%-100% of the omitted amount, together with interest and, where criminal thresholds are crossed, criminal sanctions.
Modelo 200, Box 00300 (Accounting profit before tax) Profit or loss before corporate income tax, taken from the statutory annual accounts, adjusted for accounting-local GAAP recognition of TIR transport revenues and customs-transit accruals. All worldwide income of the Spanish SL, except income exempt under Article 22 LIS for foreign permanent establishments, is subject to Spanish CIT; foreign shareholders do not file this line. Late filing before an AEAT demand triggers surcharges of 5% within three months, 10% after three to six months, 15% after six to twelve months, and 20% after twelve months plus default interest. Deliberate non-filing or under-filing is an infringement under Article 191 LGT and attracts proportional penalties of 50%-100% of the omitted amount, together with interest and, where criminal thresholds are crossed, criminal sanctions.
Modelo 200, Box 00409 (Taxable base) Accounting profit or loss plus/minus permanent and temporary tax adjustments, elimination of non-deductible expenses, application of double-tax relief, and any adjustments required by transfer pricing rules. Cross-border TIR freight routes must be priced at arm's length; intra-group trucking fees, TIR Carnet guarantees, and fuel-card clearing arrangements must not shift taxable base outside Spain. Late filing before an AEAT demand triggers surcharges of 5% within three months, 10% after three to six months, 15% after six to twelve months, and 20% after twelve months plus default interest. Deliberate non-filing or under-filing is an infringement under Article 191 LGT and attracts proportional penalties of 50%-100% of the omitted amount, together with interest and, where criminal thresholds are crossed, criminal sanctions.
Modelo 200, Box 00550 (Gross tax liability) Taxable base multiplied by the relevant rate (15%, 20%, or 25%) before the application of deductions, credits, and tax retention payments. Non-resident shareholders have no direct role in this calculation; withholding on dividends to non-residents is reported separately on Modelo 216/296 by the Spanish SL. Late filing before an AEAT demand triggers surcharges of 5% within three months, 10% after three to six months, 15% after six to twelve months, and 20% after twelve months plus default interest. Deliberate non-filing or under-filing is an infringement under Article 191 LGT and attracts proportional penalties of 50%-100% of the omitted amount, together with interest and, where criminal thresholds are crossed, criminal sanctions.
Modelo 200, Box 00652 (Net tax payable or refundable) Gross tax after domestic and treaty tax credits, deductions for reinvestment, interim Modelo 202 prepayments, and withholdings applied. If a refund results, the SL must provide a valid Spanish bank account or use the payment record code with AEAT; non-resident shareholders cannot offset their WHT against this corporate liability. Late filing before an AEAT demand triggers surcharges of 5% within three months, 10% after three to six months, 15% after six to twelve months, and 20% after twelve months plus default interest. Deliberate non-filing or under-filing is an infringement under Article 191 LGT and attracts proportional penalties of 50%-100% of the omitted amount, together with interest and, where criminal thresholds are crossed, criminal sanctions.

Transfer Pricing & Economic Substance

Master / Local File threshold: Local File and contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation are mandatory where the Spanish taxpayer's annual net turnover exceeds EUR 10,000,000, or where the aggregate fair value of related-party transactions with a single related person exceeds EUR 100,000 in the tax year. Master File documentation is required for groups with consolidated annual revenue above EUR 75,000,000; Country-by-Country Reporting applies to multinational groups with consolidated revenue of EUR 750,000,000 or more.

Economic substance scope: Spain does not operate a Caribbean-style Economic Substance Regulations code, but applies equivalent substantive requirements through Article 8 LIS (tax residence and effective management), Article 15 LIS (simulated transactions), Article 100 LIS (CFC rules), GAAR under Article 13 LGT, and the BEPS/MLI principal purpose test in DTA application. An SL engaged in TIR cross-border trucking must have real premises, employees, operational decision-making, and TIR management in Spain; otherwise profits may be recharged to Spain and treaty benefits denied.

Fatal Compliance Red Lines & Director Liability

Tax Evasion and Criminal Fraud (Criminal Code Article 305; LGT Articles 191-194)

Statutory sanction: Imprisonment of two to five years, a fine of two to six times the amount defrauded, loss of tax credits, subsidies and public contracting rights for three to six years; administrative penalty of 50%-100% of the omitted tax plus late-payment interest.

Director personal liability: Directors, de facto managers and financial signatories who ordered or participated are criminally liable. Precautionary measures in criminal proceedings may include provisional detention, travel bans and passport seizure. Under LGT Article 42.2, those who intentionally formed, managed or approved the fraudulent return are jointly and severally liable for the tax debt, penalties and interest.
Shell Company / Sham Structure and Treaty Abuse

Statutory sanction: AEAT may recharacterize the transaction under Article 15 LIS, apply the GAAR under Article 13 LGT, or invoke the CFC regime under Article 100 LIS, and assess the full Spanish CIT plus penalties of 50%-100% of the additional liability. The entity may be denied DTA benefits under the principal purpose test and suspended from using TIR Carnets by the Spanish customs authority.

Director personal liability: Corporate veil piercing is granted where the court finds the SL was a mere instrument or fraudulent vehicle. Directors and shareholders knowingly using the sham structure are personally joint and severally liable for the unpaid tax and penalties; where the concealment reaches criminal scale, imprisonment and travel restrictions may be imposed.
AML/CFT Violations and Illegal Payment Flows

Statutory sanction: Administrative sanctions under Law 10/2010 range up to EUR 1,500,000 for serious infringements and up to EUR 5,000,000 or 10% of turnover for very serious infringements, with possible closure of premises and revocation of the SL's transport licence. Criminal money laundering under Article 301 of the Spanish Criminal Code is punishable by imprisonment of six months to six years, fines and seizure of assets.

Director personal liability: Directors who knowingly use informal or offshore payment channels may be personally sanctioned under the AML Law and convicted as principals in money-laundering where funds derive from tax evasion or smuggling. Courts may order travel bans, passport seizure, the freezing of personal and corporate assets, and final disqualification from managing commercial entities.
Customs, TIR Carnet and Cross-Border Transport Violations

Statutory sanction: Customs authorities demand payment of unpaid import duties, VAT, countervailing costs and default interest. The penalty regime under the Union Customs Code and Spanish customs law may reach 100% of the evaded duties, in addition to the cancellation of the SL's TIR guarantee and exclusion from the TIR procedure.

Director personal liability: Carrier companies and their directors can be personally liable as declarants or principals for the customs debt where the infringement is intentional or grossly negligent. In smuggling cases, criminal liability under the Spanish Criminal Code applies, carrying imprisonment, fines, travel bans and civil restitution to the customs and tax authorities.
